identity.what_it_is: A sandy public swimming beach at Ferguson Point in Stanley Park, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
identity.where: Ferguson Point, Stanley Park, Vancouver, BC, Canada (49.3041N, -123.1567W per Wikipedia; 49.3034N, -123.1568W per Wikidata)
identity.warnings: Near-duplicate 'Third Beach' names exist at Middletown/Newport RI and the Olympic Peninsula WA (La Push); every fact below was checked against Ferguson Point/Stanley Park Vancouver coordinates and none was drawn from the RI or WA pages. Separately, scaffold material describing this beach as pebble/coarse-sand with no amenities or lifeguards is contradicted by every harvested source (Wikipedia, Swim Guide) - see conflicts.

spike_candidates.statement: Vancouver's own planning commission fought Ferguson Point's 1938-39 gun battery, calling it 'a favourite beauty spot,' before losing to federal wartime authority.
spike_candidates.tension: The picture-postcard beach's own parking lot was once a WWII army camp built over the city's own planners' objections.

spike_candidates.statement: Third Beach's 5-sample average hit 224 E. coli/100mL in July 2025, above the province's 200 threshold, following a June 2024 contamination investigation.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach marketed as a sandy family swim spot has a documented recent pattern of bacterial-contamination investigations, not a one-off.

spike_candidates.statement: A 2022 near-drowning at the packed weekly Third Beach drum circle got lifeguards pulled from the event and fencing installed.
spike_candidates.tension: Vancouver's most photographed sunset tradition made its own beach less safe to swim at during the event.

facts.fact: Third Beach is located at Ferguson Point within Stanley Park in Vancouver, British Columbia.
facts.quote: third beach is located at ferguson point in stanley park in vancouver , british columbia.

facts.fact: Wikidata records Third Beach's coordinates as 49°18'12.78"N, 123°9'24.26"W.
facts.quote: coordinate location 49°18'12.78"n, 123°9'24.26"w

facts.fact: Wikidata assigns Third Beach the BC Geographical Names ID 14982.
facts.quote: bc geographical names id 14982

facts.fact: Third Beach is a naturally sandy beach at Ferguson Point surrounded by old-growth forest, not a pebble beach.
facts.quote: located at ferguson point in stanley park, third beach is a naturally sandy beach surrounded by old growth forests that shield dippers and tanners from urban noise.

facts.fact: Third Beach's amenities include a concession stand, public washrooms, barbeques (with restrictions), summer lifeguards, and paid parking on the seawall.
facts.quote: amenities: concessions public washrooms barbeques allowed (subject to restrictions) lifeguards from victoria day to labour day (late may to early september) pay parking on the stanley park seawall system

facts.fact: Third Beach's water-quality reporting is managed by Swim Drink Fish - Vancouver, formerly known as Fraser Riverkeeper.
facts.quote: managed by: swim drink fish - vancouver (formerly fraser riverkeeper)

facts.fact: As of September 9, 2026, Third Beach's latest water sample met water quality standards, with results posted September 11, 2026.
facts.quote: this status is based on the latest sample, taken on september 9th, 2026

facts.fact: Siwash Rock, an adjacent landmark on the seawall between Third Beach and Prospect Point, stands 15 to 18 metres tall.
facts.quote: it is between 15 and 18 metres (49 and 59 ft) tall.

facts.fact: Siwash Rock formed about 32 million years ago when a volcanic basalt dike intruded the park's sedimentary sandstone and mudstone.
facts.quote: about 32 million years ago, a volcanic dike formed in the sedimentary rock that forms the foundation of the park

facts.fact: Mariners nicknamed Siwash Rock 'Nine Pin Rock' for its resemblance to a bowling pin.
facts.quote: it became known to mariners as nine pin rock for its resemblance to a bowling pin.

facts.fact: The Squamish name for Siwash Rock is slhx̱i7lsh, tied to a transformation legend recorded in Pauline Johnson's Legends of Vancouver.
facts.quote: the squamish name for the rock is slhx̱i7lsh

facts.fact: In 2017, Vancouver Park Board commissioner Catherine Evans introduced a motion to officially rename Siwash Rock to slhx̱í7lsh, citing its derogatory colonial origin.
facts.quote: in 2017, vancouver park board commissioner catherine evans introduced a motion to change the rock's official name to slhx̱í7lsh.

facts.fact: The Vancouver Park Board built up Third Beach over the 20th century by dredging sand from English Bay to create its shoreline.
facts.quote: the park board also built up third beach throughout the twentieth century, dredging sand from english bay to create the beach shoreline.
facts.source_title: 125 years of Stanley Park: before and after - Active History

facts.fact: Ferguson Point Battery, a WWII coastal gun battery, was established in 1939 and abandoned in 1945.
facts.quote: ferguson point battery (1939-1945) - a world war ii coastal gun battery established on ferguson point in 1939 in vancouver, british columbia. abandoned in 1945.

facts.fact: Construction of the concrete two-gun Stanley Park Battery at Ferguson Point began in mid-February 1938.
facts.quote: construction work there began in mid-february, 1938.

facts.fact: The 15th Coast Brigade's 31st Battery occupied the Ferguson Point site on August 27, 1939, as war approached.
facts.quote: the brigade's 31st battery occupied the site on 27 august, 1939.

facts.fact: The battery's guns and most of its buildings were removed in September 1945.
facts.quote: stanley park's guns and most of the buildings were removed in september 1945.

facts.fact: Ferguson Point's military use began in 1914, when a temporary two-gun battery was set up near Siwash Rock over fears of a German East Asia Squadron attack.
facts.quote: ferguson point's military use started in 1914, when a temporary gun battery was set up near siwash rock, manned by naval reservists with two 4-inch caliber guns
facts.source_title: The forgotten guns of Ferguson Point, Stanley Park

facts.fact: Vancouver's Town Planning Commission opposed siting the gun battery at Ferguson Point, calling it a favourite beauty spot in the park.
facts.quote: the town planning commission, however, did not approve of the use of ferguson point for the battery, calling it "a favourite beauty spot in the park."

facts.fact: The Vancouver Sun editorialized that the battery could become a permanent blot on the scenic beauty of the area.
facts.quote: the vancouver sun joined the opposition and stated that the gun battery could become "a permanent blot on the scenic beauty of the area."

facts.fact: A soldiers' camp tied to the battery occupied what is now the Third Beach parking lot.
facts.quote: a soldiers' camp occupied the present third beach parking lot.

facts.fact: The Vancouver Park Board won its fight for full restoration of Ferguson Point to parkland in April 1948, after which the gun emplacements were levelled and buried.
facts.quote: in april 1948 the board won this battle.

facts.fact: The Teahouse restaurant at Ferguson Point occupies the site of the WWII battery's former officers' mess.
facts.quote: ferguson point teahouse formerly the officer's mess of ferguson point battery

facts.fact: A historical marker at Ferguson Point records the site was manned during WWII (1939-1945) by three Royal Canadian Artillery batteries: the 31st, 58th, and 85th Heavy.
facts.quote: this area was the site of a coast defence fort manned during ww ii 1939-1945 by the royal canadian artillery batteries 31st heavy 58th heavy 85th heavy

facts.fact: Ferguson Point sits on federally owned land that has been leased to the City of Vancouver as parkland for a nominal sum since 1887.
facts.quote: this federally-owned land had been leased to the city for a nominal sum since 1887.

facts.fact: Third Beach's five most recent water samples averaged 224 E. coli/100 mL as of mid-July 2025, exceeding the province's 200 geometric-mean threshold.
facts.quote: third beach is under advisory for a different reason: its five most recent water samples averaged 224 e. coli/100 ml, surpassing the provincial geometric mean threshold of 200.
facts.source_title: Several Vancouver beaches under advisory due to E. coli spike - Daily Hive

facts.fact: In June 2024, Vancouver Coastal Health placed Sunset, Third, and Second beaches under a beach action value investigation due to repeated bacteria spikes.
facts.quote: in june 2024, vch placed sunset, third beach, and second beach under a beach action value investigation due to repeated spikes in bacteria levels.
facts.source_title: Several Vancouver beaches under advisory due to E. coli spike - Daily Hive

facts.fact: VCH's 2023 update to its beach action value system means a single sample exceeding 235 E. coli/100 mL now triggers an investigation, versus the prior 400 threshold.
facts.quote: the key change is if a single sample exceeds 235 e.coli/100 ml (as opposed to 400 e.coli/100 ml prior to 2023), a contamination investigation, and resampling will be triggered.
facts.source_title: Public Beach Water Quality - Vancouver Coastal Health

facts.fact: Third Beach is sampled weekly from May 10 through October 10 each season.
facts.quote: third beach is sampled weekly from may 10th to october 10th.

facts.fact: The weekly Tuesday drum circle at Third Beach was set to celebrate its 18th anniversary in June 2023, implying an origin around 2005.
facts.quote: next week, the drum circle will celebrate its 18th anniversary.
facts.source_title: Bumpin' Third Beach: drum circle throng returns - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The weekly drum circle came under scrutiny after a 2022 near-drowning in which lifeguards reportedly had trouble reaching the victim through the crowd.
facts.quote: the weekly drum circle became the subject of scrutiny last summer after someone came close to drowning and had to be pulled from the water.
facts.source_title: Bumpin' Third Beach: drum circle throng returns - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The near-drowning incident led to lifeguards being pulled from Third Beach on Tuesday evenings, fencing added, and temporary police patrols.
facts.quote: the incident led to lifeguards being pulled from the beach on tuesday evenings, fencing added to the beach, and police temporarily patrolling the event.
facts.source_title: Bumpin' Third Beach: drum circle throng returns - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The drum circle, formally named Brahm's Tams, runs every Tuesday evening from May through September near Ferguson Point.
facts.quote: season dates every tuesday evening from may through september 2026 weather permitting
facts.source_title: Brahm's Tams Drum Circle 2026 at Third Beach - Vancouver Page

facts.fact: Organizers describe Brahm's Tams as one of the city's most photographed and shared weekly summer gatherings, running for more than two decades.
facts.quote: brahm's tams has become one of the city's most photographed and shared weekly summer gatherings.
facts.source_title: Brahm's Tams Drum Circle 2026 at Third Beach - Vancouver Page

facts.fact: Community guidelines for the drum circle prohibit open alcohol or drug use, dogs on the beach, and open fires.
facts.quote: no open alcohol or drug use no dogs on the beach no open fires
facts.source_title: Brahm's Tams Drum Circle 2026 at Third Beach - Vancouver Page

facts.fact: A storm surge and king tide on January 7, 2022 heavily damaged the seawall between Third Beach and Lions Gate Bridge; the final repaired section reopened April 27, 2022.
facts.quote: members of the public are now free to roam between vancouver's third beach and lions gate bridge, an area heavily damaged by extreme winds and a king tide on jan. 7.
facts.source_title: Final section of Stanley Park seawall reopens after storm damage repair - Global News

facts.fact: The Stanley Park seawall repair following the January 2022 storm was estimated to cost $1.5 million.
facts.quote: the cost of repairs on the seawall is estimated to be $1.5 million
facts.source_title: Final section of Stanley Park seawall reopens after storm damage repair - Global News

facts.fact: The January 2022 storm damage collapsed the seawall in several areas along the 3.5-kilometre stretch between Second Beach and Lions Gate Bridge.
facts.quote: which collapsed in several areas in the 3.5-kilometre stretch between second beach and lions gate bridge.
facts.source_title: Final section of Stanley Park seawall reopens after storm damage repair - Global News

conflicts: Scaffold material describes Third Beach as pebble/coarse-sand with no amenities or lifeguards; Swim Guide (F04, F05) and Wikipedia instead document a naturally sandy beach with a concession stand, washrooms, and summer lifeguards - every harvested source contradicts the scaffold's framing.

The Ferguson Point historical marker (F24) names three RCA batteries (31st/58th/85th Heavy) manning the site 1939-45, while Vancouver Gunners' narrative (F15-F17, F19-F22) centers on the 31st Battery alone without mentioning the 58th or 85th.
